title: StatusJsonOutput
description: Top-level envelope for `rwv status --json`. Matches the convention adopted by doctor (`$schema` + `violations`) and sync (`$schema` + `outcomes`): `{ "$schema": "<url>", "repos": [<RepoStatus>, ...] }`.

aligned.description: The branch each project's workspace last aligned its members for.

backups.description: The backups each repo holds, with what each keeps that no branch reaches. Only repos that hold one.

judged.description: Each repo judged on the axes `rwv status` reads, with that state's choices: `alignment` (a member not in its expected state, or carrying a fact such as `checkout`, and the project repo against the aligned branch), and `push-branch` where the branch needs attention: behind, diverged, gone with commits of its own, with a foreign upstream or with no push target. A branch that is ahead of its push branch is the ordinary state of work in progress and has no line; the per-repo `relation` and `operator_branches` carry what is unpublished. Empty, not absent, when none stands apart.

op.description: The sync/land op parked at this workspace, or leased to one elsewhere, if any. Absent when no op is in progress — the same disclosure the in-flight refusal makes, before an operator has to attempt a mutation to learn it.

operator_branches.description: Each member's local branch holding unpushed commits that nothing else accounts for: checked out nowhere, named after no recorded weave branch of any project here, and no declared branch of that member.

records.description: Each project's checked-out branch with its record and the branches that land into it, read in memory from the records as last fetched. A project whose repo is not on a branch has none.

resolution.description: Resolved workspace coordinates (weave root, optional workweave identity, project). Absent when no project is resolved.

unreadable_op.description: Why the operation record this workspace holds, or the one its lease names, cannot be read, as the refusal every other verb prints says it, naming the verb that ends the operation. Absent when there is no such record or it reads.

unreadable_projects.description: Projects whose `rwv.toml` or `rwv.lock` did not load: none of their repos is in `repos`.

AlignedStatus.description: What a project's workspace last aligned its members for.

branch.description: The branch it last aligned for; absent where none is recorded or the workspace is detached.

detached.description: Whether the workspace was made detached.

unreadable.description: Why the workspace state, which reads as absent, could not be read.

Axis.description: What a refusal judged a repo on. Its token is the kind `rwv explain` serves; the order here is the order a repo's lines print in.

Projects sharing a member that record different `history` for it.
Where a workspace's checkouts sit against where the checked-out branch's record says they should.
A branch rwv never rewrites, renames or deletes.
A project repo whose lock merge driver is not set up as this release sets it up.
A project commit `rwv cherry-pick` cannot port as it stands.

oneOf.description: Made before a rebase rewrote the branch.
The tip of a remote-tracking branch a fetch found rewritten.
The branch's one slot for the tip `rwv abort` last reset it from; the next abort that resets the branch overwrites it.
The checkout's one slot for the working copy `rwv abort` last discarded on it; the next abort that discards one there overwrites it.

held.description: The commits the backup holds that no branch reaches, newest first.

mark.description: `rebased` for a branch a rebase rewrote; absent for any other.

redundant.description: A branch reaches everything the backup holds, so dropping it loses nothing.

dependents.description: The branches whose records name this one as their target.

id.description: The choice's id on the axis's page; null for one it does not number.

run.description: The commands, one per line, as the terminal prints them.

where.description: The directory it must run in; null where it runs here or names its own directory.

CommitId.description: A full commit id: 40 lowercase hex digits, or 64 in a SHA-256 repository.

FactKind.description: A fact about a judged repo. Facts are reported; they never select a choice.

choices.description: What this state can run, in the order the page lists it.

workspace.description: The workspace the repo was judged in, when that is not the one the verb ran in.

LockRelation.description:
Relation between the current branch tip and the lock SHA.

The two clone-health variants (`Missing` / `Unreachable`) name distinct failure modes, neither of which is `NoLock`:

- `Missing` — the clone directory is absent from disk entirely (out-of-band `rm -rf`, never fetched, etc.). The lock entry may be fine; the repair verb is a re-clone / `rwv update`.

- `Unreachable` — the clone directory exists but the SHA pinned in the lock is not present in the local object store (history rewritten, shallow clone, object pruned). The repair is `git fetch` in that clone, which re-materializes the missing object; `rwv update` does not fetch into a clone that is present.

Neither state should be attributed to the lock file itself — surfacing them as `no-lock` misdirects operators at the wrong repair path.

oneOf.description: Clone directory is absent from disk (out-of-band removal, never fetched). Repair: re-clone / `rwv update`.

Clone directory exists but the locked SHA is not in the local object store (history rewritten, shallow clone, object pruned). Repair: `git fetch` in that clone to materialize the missing object; `rwv update` does not fetch into a clone that is present.

MidOperation.description: The operation a repository is stopped in: a conflict being resolved, or a bisect.

Mode.description: How a weave branch is used.

oneOf.description: Work onto a target branch: its `owned` and `fork` members sit on branches named after it.
Members sit on the branches its member entries declare.

OpPhase.description:
Current phase of the in-flight operation.

Phases are listed in execution order.

```text guard → mark → savepoint → replay → relock → advance-target → retire → cleanup (land only)   (--retire only) ```

The persisted phase is always the phase in progress. Every phase is idempotent and re-runnable from the record alone.

oneOf.description: Project repo, then member repos: Phase 1' and Phase 2.
Regenerate and commit `rwv.lock` (today's Phase 3). On completion, converged tips are written into the owner record.
FF-advance every target repo to its converged tip (land only).
Merged-check then workweave removal (`--retire` only).

OpStatus.description:
The in-flight op recorded at this workspace (owner) or the workspace this one leases to (owner elsewhere), disclosed read-only on `rwv status`.

The record minus its tip table (`converged_tips`): that is replay bookkeeping an operator deciding `--continue` vs `abort` doesn't need. `verb` and `phase` are the op-state crate's own types, not a re-encoding of them — a second vocabulary for the same facts is the thing this disclosure must not become.

owner.description: Workspace holding the full op record (`.rwv-op`) — the workspace `--continue`/`abort` must run from. Equal to the reporting workspace unless this workspace only holds a lease.

target.description: The workspace that has the landing's target checked out; absent where it is checked out nowhere and the landing moves it as refs.

OpVerb.description: Which top-level verb started this op.

oneOf.description: `rwv sync`: a feature takes in its target, or a branch merges `--from`.
`rwv land`: compose in the source, then fast-forward the target.
`rwv pull` with `--merge-upstream` or `--reset-to-upstream`.
`rwv update --remote` with `--merge-upstream` or `--reset-to-upstream`.
`rwv cherry-pick`: copy each member's range of a project commit, then the project commit with the relock.

OperatorBranch.description: A member's local branch holding unpushed commits that nothing else accounts for.

gone_upstream.description: The branch takes in from a remote branch its remote no longer has.

unpushed.description: How many commits no remote-tracking branch reaches.

ParentInfo.description:
Recorded-parent exposure for a per-repo status entry.

Parent identity comes from the workweave's `.rwv-workweave` marker (`parent:`), never from the branch name: a workweave's branch is the flat `<project>--<name>`, which names no parent, and adoption can re-point the parent to primary. Consumers that need the parent must read this field.

`path` is the recorded parent workspace path (identical for every repo in the workweave). `tip` is this specific repo's parent tip — the SHA that `git rev-parse HEAD` yields in the parent's checkout of the SAME repo — or `None` when the parent has no checkout of this repo (or HEAD is unreadable). The tip is what `git log <parent-tip>..HEAD` needs to compute the workweave's unique commits without re-deriving branch layout.

path.description: Recorded parent workspace path (from the `.rwv-workweave` marker).

tip.description: This repo's HEAD in the parent's checkout, if resolvable.

RecordOutput.description: One weave branch's record, as `rwv branch list --json` carries it.

target_branch.description: The branch the feature lands into.

oneOf.description: The branch has no record here.
Two writers recorded the branch differently; both values are listed.
The entry does not read as a record.
The branch's target chain returns to it.

path.description: The repo as `rwv backup drop` names it: its workspace-relative path, or `projects/<name>` for the project repo.

lock_pinned_by_name.description: `true` when the lock entry holds a tag or branch name rather than a commit id; `rwv lock` records the commit id.

parent.description: Recorded parent (path + per-repo parent tip) when CWD is a workweave; `None` in the primary weave (no marker, hence no recorded parent).

Resolution.description:
Resolved workspace coordinates for `--json` output and the plugin env-var envelope.

Carries `workspace` (primary root abs path), `workweave` (the `<project>--<name>` identity the registry records), `project` (resolved project name), and `workweave_unregistered`. No `kind` or `location` field: the checkout is one of three states, and two of them are already carried by `workweave`'s presence.

The third state needs a field of its own. A workweave whose directory no registry entry names has no identity, so `workweave` is absent for it — and absent is what the primary looks like. Without `workweave_unregistered` the two serialize identically, and a consumer reading the documented meaning of that absence is told, positively, that it is at the primary checkout.

Results only — provenance (which chain step resolved the project, which flag addressed the workspace) is deliberately excluded: anything in default `--json` output becomes depended on, and the assertion use case needs the result, not the mechanism. Provenance appears only in the human-facing "target:" line printed to stderr.

Isomorphic to the plugin env-var envelope (`RWV_WORKSPACE`/`RWV_WORKWEAVE`/`RWV_WORKWEAVE_UNREGISTERED`/`RWV_PROJECT`): both surfaces are pure projections of the one resolution of the workspace, never independently computed.

project.description: Resolved project name; absent when the workspace resolved but no project did (a primary with no project selected).

workweave.description:
Workweave identity (`<project>--<name>`), as the primary-side registry records it.

Absent at the primary, and absent for a workweave whose directory no registry entry names — identity is by record, so an unregistered workweave has no identity to report and rwv will not spell one from the directory name. Those two absences are told apart by `workweave_unregistered`, not by this field.

workweave_unregistered.description:
`true` when the invocation resolved into a workweave whose directory no registry entry names, so `workweave` above is absent for a reason that is not "this is the primary".

Serialized only in that state, so the primary and a registered workweave emit exactly the bytes they emitted before this field existed. `rwv doctor --fix` registers such a directory, after which this is absent and `workweave` carries the identity.

Role.description:
How freely code in this repo may be modified within the owning project.

**Naming.** The variant is spelled `owned` everywhere on the wire (the manifest, `--role` CLI arguments, `--json` output). The legacy `primary` spelling — used before the rename — is **not** accepted by the parser.
